findings.title: Credential scan authorizes deeply nested secret values
findings.evidence: preflight.mjs:318-344 returns null once depth exceeds 8. A valid request containing a credential at ten nested levels returned ok=true, authorized ACP-002, and condition 7 reported "value never read".

findings.title: Permission parser can judge another job's permissions
findings.evidence: writerPermissionsFromWorkflow searches for any permissions block after the writer job without stopping at the next job. Removing the writer block from the committed workflow made it parse attest's {contents:"read"}; runPreflight then returned ok=true and authorized ACP-002 although the writer permissions were absent.

findings.title: Retry ceiling is bypassed by a fresh dispatch
findings.evidence: The only retry accounting is GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT (workflow lines 179-182). A new workflow_dispatch for the same item/SHA starts a new run at attempt 1; no board or durable counter limits repeated dispatches. max_retries:0 therefore does not bound total writer invocations.

findings.title: Writer can rewrite its own post-write scope enforcement
findings.evidence: ACP-002's declared scope includes scope-guard.mjs and item-scopes.json. The writer has unrestricted Write/Edit tools, and workflow lines 295-327 execute those working-tree versions only after the writer finishes. It can weaken the guard/declaration, modify ACP-003, and have the weakened guard approve the result.

findings.title: Branch fence is mutable before the token-bearing push
findings.evidence: The scope check observes only git-status paths and does not validate or restore .git/config. Write/Edit remain available during the writer step; the final push later supplies github.token through http.extraheader. Git URL rewriting in modified repository metadata can redirect that token-bearing push, defeating the asserted branch fence and exposing a token capable of direct contents writes.

findings.title: Reverse-proof coverage remains incomplete
findings.evidence: Condition 5 has no removal/inversion proof. The condition-2 proof at preflight.test.mjs:346-351 asserts only that checks[1].ok becomes true, not that result.ok is true and authorized is non-null, despite the suite's stated end-to-end proof standard.

findings.title: Latest repaired SHA lacks verifiable cloud attestation
findings.evidence: The board records the post-repair attestation run 31959714663 as FAILED and its current next_action still requires CI and PR attestation before freezing a new candidate. No successful cloud attestation for 821a44b0 is present in the immutable candidate.

findings.title: Focused suite could not be independently completed in this sandbox
findings.evidence: node --test control-plane/*.test.mjs exited 1 because kernel.test.mjs's CLI test received EPERM spawning Node. The preflight and scope-guard suites passed, and node control-plane/kernel.mjs check exited 0 with ok=true, but the required full command is not independently green.

summary: FAIL: hostile inputs can bypass credential and permission checks; retry accounting is not durable; and mutable post-write enforcement permits foreign-item changes. The latest SHA also lacks independently verifiable cloud attestation, while the full focused suite was unverified due the read-only sandbox's child-process restriction.
